title: Build carrier label requests from one set of settings

blocks.text: The warehouse asks a carrier's API for shipping labels. `LabelRequests` holds the settings every request shares (the API's address, a timeout, the token and the `Accept` header) in one `HttpRequest.Builder`, and builds the requests that a separate sender sends. The carrier uses the `X-Request-Id` header to recognise a label requested twice, so each label request must carry exactly one id, its own, and status requests must carry none.

Finish `label(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/LabelRequests.java`: it returns a POST of the given JSON with the shared settings and the given request id. `status(...)` already works. Nothing is sent over the network; the tests read the requests you build. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a label request is a POST of the JSON to the label API with the shared timeout and headers and its own request id
a label request built after others carries its own request id and no earlier one
building a label request leaves the shared settings as they were, so a later status request carries no request id

origin.section: HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers

concepts: HttpRequest.Builder.copy() gives each request its own builder with the template's state, so nothing added for one request reaches the template or the next request.
